chunks: Crude, and above all, mean and infamous,

key_terms.زَنِيمٍ: Mean, infamous, or one who commits fornication (often used for character)
key_terms.عُتُلٍ: Crude, stubborn, or difficult in character

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'Zanim' mean in the context of the Pen chapter?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, these epithets describe the moral degradation of the disbelievers, with 'utulin' denoting their coarse, unrefined nature and 'zanimin' indicating their status as despised or infamous figures. This characterization underscores the spiritual blindness of those who reject divine guidance, contrasting their inner corruption with the clarity of the Prophets.
